page: Amazon Web Services c8g.2xlarge is an arm64 compute-optimized virtual machine operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The instance is powered by an eight-core AWS Neoverse-V2 ARMv9 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz, delivering dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core. The CPU configuration provides 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AES cryptographic extensions. It is provisioned with 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 2.0 GB per-core compute-optimized memory ratio. No local disk storage or GPU accelerators are bundled with this instance type, and baseline network throughput is rated at 4 Gbps.

Performance profiles show competitive throughput in memory-intensive operations. In uncached large-block memory read evaluations, the instance achieved 188.91 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25% of tested configurations. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 14.22 GB/sec, also testing within the top quartile. General compute benchmarks placed it firmly within average tiers, recording 13,647.2 on stress-ng multi-core and 9,878.0 on Geekbench multi-core. Relative weaknesses appeared in the PassMark encryption test with a score of 1,509.87 and medium-model 7B LLM prompt processing at 15.58 tokens per second, both falling into lower percentiles due to architecture and memory constraints.

The hardware configuration provides strong qualitative efficiency for dedicated compute tasks that rely on predictable execution without hyperthreading interference. The absence of local NVMe storage requires external network-attached volumes, making the platform best matched to compute-bound rather than I/O-heavy local disk workloads. Given its balanced multi-core metrics, high memory read bandwidth, and 18.14 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, the c8g.2xlarge fits software compilation, web serving, in-memory caching layers, and general compute-optimized batch processing.

Featuring dedicated physical execution with one thread per core, the system pairs 16.0 GB of memory with an 8-vCPU allocation, establishing a 2.0 GB per-core compute-focused profile. Built on the Nitro hypervisor, the instance delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps and excludes local storage and GPU hardware. The instance is suited for batch processing, web serving, software compilation, and in-memory caches.
